opus-5.5.text:
I think a lot of it comes from history and culture. NYU has a really deep legacy in this field. Yann LeCun has been here for a long time, and the whole lineage of convolutional networks and deep learning has roots at NYU. When I was deciding where to go after industry, that history meant something to me. It's not just a name on a building. There's a real intellectual tradition of people who believed in neural networks back when it wasn't fashionable at all.

Then there's the environment. NYU is in New York City, which is a very different place from a typical college town. You're surrounded by finance, media, art, medicine, and a lot of industry labs. That diversity matters for AI now, because the field isn't only about building models anymore. It's about how they connect to the real world. Being in the city gives students and researchers that exposure naturally.

Culturally, the group here is fairly open and interdisciplinary. Computer science, the Center for Data Science, Courant's mathematics tradition, and neuroscience and psychology all sit close together. If you care about things like visual representation learning, world models, or how intelligence actually works, which is what I care about, those conversations happen very naturally.

To be honest, compared with the very largest programs, NYU isn't the biggest in terms of compute or headcount. But I don't think that's necessarily a disadvantage. Academia shouldn't try to compete with big tech on scale. Our advantage is that we can take on riskier, longer-term questions, the things industry may not prioritize because they don't pay off in the next quarter. NYU has a culture that tolerates that kind of exploration, and I think that's where a university can really make a difference in AI right now.

r002.rationale: It mentions NYU's AI history and computer science, but does not contrast a concentration of outstanding AI faculty with computer science not being an institutional strength.

fable-5.1.text:
Thanks for having me. There are a few things that come together at NYU that I think are hard to replicate.

The first is history. The Courant Institute has been one of the strongest math and computing departments in the world for decades, and Yann LeCun has been at NYU since 2003. He built the deep learning culture here long before it was fashionable. People like Rob Fergus, Kyunghyun Cho, Joan Bruna, and Yann created an environment where researchers were doing representation learning and neural networks when most of the field had moved on to other things. That kind of institutional memory matters. The students and faculty here never had to be convinced that deep learning works; they were living it.

The second is the people. NYU is relatively small compared with places like Stanford or Berkeley, but the density of talent in machine learning, computer vision, and language is very high. And because it is small, the walls between groups are thin. I can walk down the hall and talk to someone working on theory, or on language models, or on neuroscience, and that kind of mixing is where a lot of good ideas come from. When I joined, it felt less like a department and more like a lab with many PIs.

The third is New York City itself. This is something people underestimate. New York is not just finance and media anymore. Google, Meta, Microsoft, and most of the frontier AI labs now have serious research presence here. Yann's own group at Meta FAIR is in the same city. So students can collaborate with industry without leaving, and we attract people who want to live in a real city rather than a suburb. That diversity of people and ideas is a real advantage for AI, which at this point is as much about culture and taste as it is about hardware.

And finally, I think NYU has a good attitude toward research. There is a lot of pressure in the field right now to chase scale and follow what the big labs are doing. At NYU there is still room to ask slightly uncomfortable questions: are we actually building systems that understand the world, or are we fitting benchmarks? Yann has been very vocal about this, and it gives junior faculty like me permission to work on things that may take longer to pay off, like visual representation learning, world models, and the fundamentals of how vision and language should interact.

So it is a combination of a deep history, a dense and open community, a city that is becoming an AI hub, and a culture that values thinking a bit differently. I feel very lucky to be here.

astra-6.text:
I think NYU is well positioned because it brings together strong foundations in AI and a lot of intellectual diversity. You have people thinking about learning from very different perspectives, and that creates opportunities to question assumptions and explore new directions.

Being in New York also helps. AI connects to so many areas—science, medicine, art, business—and you’re surrounded by people working on those problems. For me, the exciting part is the combination: an environment where you can pursue fundamental research while staying close to questions that matter outside the lab.

r001.rationale: The response says AI connects to areas including science, medicine, art, and business, presenting it as a link across disciplines.

r002.rationale: The response does not state that NYU has a concentration of outstanding AI faculty or contrast that with computer science not being an institutional strength.

sol-6.1.text:
I think NYU has a really strong combination of people and intellectual freedom. You have researchers thinking about the foundations of machine learning, but also people working on vision, language, robotics, and how these systems connect to the world. That creates opportunities to exchange ideas across different areas.

And being in New York helps. You’re surrounded by different industries, different disciplines, and people asking very different questions. For AI, that diversity is valuable. You want an environment where people can challenge the prevailing approach and explore ideas that might take time to pay off. I think that’s an important strength for a university.
